## Diverging Signals
- **Price is worse, scores are unchanged.** Every lens was already near its floor, so a 6.5% TQQQ drop shows up as stress inside the lenses, not as a new score. The −11 understates how fast things moved today.
- **Neutralizer met, yet stocks fell.** Brent is under $100 and the 10Y is under 5.10%. Those were the relief conditions, and they did not hold the market up. Credit and volatility are what matter now.
- **RSI rose while price fell.** RSI is 34.4, above the 31.6 of the prior read, even after a 6.54% drop. Oversold readings are not a bounce signal here. Treat the RSI as lagging.
- **Put/call is calm, volatility is not.** Put/call is 0.54 while VIX/VIX3M is in backwardation and VVIX is 127. Traders are not buying heavy put protection on TQQQ, yet index volatility says stress is rising. This split often means the fear is not yet fully priced.
- **Option cost versus movement.** IV/HV is 0.84 (options cost about 16% less than the stock has actually been moving). Premium is thin for the risk even with VXN at 36.48.

- Market structure: **DOWNTURN.** Spot ($49.01) is 32.4% under the $72.53 4-week high ($49.01 / $72.53 = 0.676), past the 20% line. VXN is 36.48, past the 25 line. Both legs are met. Spot is 0.4% above the 4-week low ($49.01 / $48.81 = 1.004), far short of the 30% line for RALLY.
- Trend: below the 50DMA by 29.34% and below the 200DMA by 25.2%. Spot is 44.13% under the 52-week high and 31.9% above the 52-week low.
- Volatility & premium environment: VXN is 36.48 (+10.14%), within 6.0% of its 52-week high of 38.66. Chain ATM IV is 0.87 and IV/HV is 0.84 (HV20 103.2%). IV/HV under 1 means options cost less than the stock has actually been moving, so sellers get no extra cushion. Chain IV of 87% is about 20% under the ~109% implied by the 3x-VXN rule of thumb (estimate only). VVIX at 127.10 says volatility itself is unstable.
- Put-selling context: HOSTILE. The stage is 5, all seven lenses are bearish, spot sits 0.4% above its 4-week low, and both credit lines are broken. The volatility curve is back in backwardation and VXN is near its 52-week high. IV/HV of 0.84 says the premium is cheap for the movement. A one-week expected move of about ±15% is wide against a stock this close to a fresh low. Context only — no strikes, expiries or sizes.
